title: Without Coercion: the Officer of Przemysl and the Ground Adjoining the Mountain of Truth
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Kronstadt and the Eighteenth of August

stops.name: Kronstadt, birth under the Burzenland mountains
stops.date_confidence: attested [A]: de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)', gives 13 August 1875 at Kronstadt (Brasov) and names both parents, Carl Samuel Gräser and Charlotte Caroline née Pelzer. The article's Personendaten register the full name as Gräser, Carl Samuel Josef. The research pool's coordinate 45.6579/25.6012 sits about 1.9 km northeast of the historic centre and is not used; the pin is Piata Sfatului, inherited byte-identical from gusto_graeser.journey.json. No birth address is documented.
stops.campa: A son is born on the thirteenth of August to Carl Samuel Gräser and Charlotte Caroline, born Pelzer, in the Saxon town of Kronstadt under the Burzenland mountains, at the eastern rim of Austria-Hungary. The registers enter him as Carl Samuel Josef, after his father. The town has German schools, a black church of blackened stone, and a frontier two hours' walk away beyond which the Habsburg empire stops. He is the first of three sons. He will wear an imperial uniform for seven years of his life, beginning at nineteen, and he will live to forty-one.
suggested_refs: The German-speaking Saxon town of Kronstadt in the Burzenland, birthplace of all three Gräser brothers

stops.name: Kronstadt, the two younger brothers
stops.date_confidence: attested [A]: Gustav 'Gusto' Gräser born 16 February 1879 at Kronstadt (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'), died 1958; Ernst H. Graeser born 1884, died 1944, painter and graphic artist (de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'). The research pool's undated '1879' is corrected to the day. The pool's further claim that Gusto was 'later his collaborator at Ohne Zwang' is unsupported and dropped: Ohne Zwang was founded with Leopold Ferdinand in the Przemysl garrison and no source associates Gusto with it.
stops.campa: Gustav is born on the sixteenth of February 1879 into the same house, and Ernst follows in 1884. Gustav will take the name Gusto, refuse salt, money and capital letters, and be the one the century writes about. Ernst will paint and make prints. Karl, four years older than one and nine older than the other, is the brother who holds land, signs papers, and stays legible to a registry office long enough to be entered in one. Ernst dies in 1944 and Gusto in 1958. Karl, the eldest of the three, goes first, in 1916.
suggested_refs: The prints and paintings of Ernst H. Graeser (1884-1944), the youngest brother

stops.name: Kronstadt, the father's death
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] for the date: de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)', gives Carl Samuel Gräser as 13 June 1839 to 16 May 1894, and in the same sentence the mother Charlotte Caroline as 1853 to 1920. The research pool carried the year only. No place of death is given by the source; the family town is used as the pin and is not itself attested for this event. The three-month gap to Karl's entry into regimental service is a real adjacency that no source connects to the death.
stops.campa: Carl Samuel Gräser dies on the sixteenth of May, fifty-four years old. His widow Charlotte Caroline is forty-one and will outlive her eldest son by four years. Karl is eighteen. Three months later he is in uniform. No source joins the two facts and none rules the join out, and no source gives the place of the father's death either. In the house at Kronstadt after May there is a widow of forty-one, a boy of fifteen and a boy of ten, and by August the eldest son has gone to the regiment.
suggested_refs: The Gräser household at Kronstadt after May 1894, a widow and three sons

stops.name: Kronstadt, the eighteenth of August
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] for the date: 'vom 18. August 1894 bis zum 16. September 1901 Oberleutnant im k.u.k. Infanterieregiment Erzherzog Ludwig Salvator Nr. 58' (de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'). Correction to the research pool, which read this as an entry rank: the sentence gives the span of service and the rank recorded for it, and he was nineteen on this date, so he cannot have entered as Oberleutnant. No place is given for the enlistment; the family town is the pin, set to order the segment.
stops.campa: He enters the k.u.k. Infanterieregiment Erzherzog Ludwig Salvator Nr. 58 five days after his nineteenth birthday. The service will run seven years and one month to the day, and the rank standing on the record for it is Oberleutnant. That is the whole of what survives of his military career in any accessible source: one regiment, two dates, one rank. No campaign, no promotion, no reprimand, no leave papers, no letters home. Whether he was any good at soldiering, nothing on the record says.
suggested_refs: The service record of k.u.k. Infanterieregiment 'Erzherzog Ludwig Salvator' Nr. 58, 1894-1901

stops.name: Przemysl, the fortress garrison
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] that he was stationed at Przemysl, but over-read in the research pool. De.wikipedia says he served there 'unter anderem', among other places, within the 1894-1901 span; it does not say he was garrisoned there for all seven years and gives no year for the posting itself. 1896 is set only to order the segment, and no other station is named by any source consulted. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from gusto_graeser.journey.json.
stops.campa: Przemysl in Galicia is the empire's great eastern fortress, a ring of works thrown around a garrison town on the San, built against Russia and manned by conscripts out of a dozen languages. Gräser is posted there at some point within his seven years. The source says among other places and then names no other. What the posting consisted of is described nowhere: drill, inspection, the mess, the parade square, the timetable of a peacetime army with nothing to do but rehearse itself.
suggested_refs: The Austro-Hungarian fortress ring at Przemysl on the San

stops.name: Przemysl, the Hauptmann who had been an archduke
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] that Leopold Ferdinand of Austria-Tuscany commanded in the Przemysl garrison and that de.wikipedia's 'Leopold Wölfling' calls Gräser 'einer seiner Offiziere in der Garnison von Przemysl', crediting Gräser with introducing him to Lebensreform ideas. Two corrections to the research pool: he was not a fellow officer but Gräser's superior, a Hauptmann; and he was not yet Leopold Wölfling and had not renounced his titles, which he did by letter from Zürich to the Emperor on 14 December 1902, marrying Wilhelmine Adamovic in 1903. Year set to order the segment. The narration that both men held the drill in contempt is Wikipedia's own sentence, 'Beide empfanden tiefe Verachtung für den soldatischen Drill', not a quoted document.
stops.campa: The Hauptmann over him is Leopold Ferdinand of Austria-Tuscany, grandson of an emperor, brother of a queen of Saxony, a serving officer carrying a Habsburg archduke's rank and a Habsburg archduke's boredom. Gräser is one of his officers. It is the subordinate who does the teaching here: the life-reform literature, the vegetarian argument, the case against the drill, all of it reaches the archduke from a lieutenant out of Kronstadt. Both of them, the record says, held the soldier's drill in deep contempt.
suggested_refs: Leopold Ferdinand of Austria-Tuscany, who renounced his titles in 1902 and took the name Leopold Wölfling

stops.name: Przemysl, the association without coercion
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] that Gräser and Leopold founded a Verein named Ohne Zwang, Gräser as Geschäftsführer and Leopold as Präsident, and that the name alluded to the ideas of Charles Fourier, whose philosophy Gräser esteemed (de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)', citing Bollmann 2017, p. 25). No source dates the founding: the research pool's 1899 is invented and c. 1898 here is a placeholder inside the shared service. No founding place is stated either; Przemysl is used because that is where the two men served together. Single-sourced: Wölfling's own article does not mention Ohne Zwang at all. The quotation is Fourier's formulation, quoted by Bollmann, and is NOT Gräser's words, against the research pool's attribution.
stops.campa: Inside the fortress the two of them found an association and call it Ohne Zwang, Without Coercion. Gräser runs it as business manager; the archduke is its president. The name comes from Charles Fourier, the Frenchman sixty years dead who drew up the phalanstery in which nobody is made to do anything, and whose philosophy Gräser esteems. The two men signing it are serving officers of an army whose whole trade is the lawful giving of orders. No source gives the year the association was founded, the room it was founded in, or whether anybody else ever joined it.
stops.quote: Alles, was sich auf Zwang gründet, ist hinfällig und Mangel an Geist
stops.quote_source: Charles Fourier, quoted in Stefan Bollmann, Monte Verità 1900 (DVA, München 2017), p. 25, as the phrase behind the association's name; cited on de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'
suggested_refs: Charles Fourier's phalanstery, whose principle gave the Przemysl association its name
sources: Stefan Bollmann, Monte Verità 1900 (DVA, München 2017), p. 25

stops.name: Przemysl, seven years and one sentence
stops.date_confidence: gap statement [R]. No letter, order book, diary or brother officer's anecdote by or about Gräser from the 1894-1901 service was located in any accessible source. The German sentence widely attached to his name, 'die geistlose Zurichtung des Körpers wie des Verstandes zu militärischen Zwecken', does NOT appear in de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)', checked against the full wikitext export, last edited 20 May 2026; it is not reproduced here as his words. Year set to order the segment.
stops.campa: Seven years of a man's twenties, and the paper holds a regiment, a rank, two dates and one fortress named among others. No letter survives out of the garrison, no order book with his hand in it, no anecdote from a brother officer. A polished German sentence about the mindless regimentation of body and mind circulates attached to his name; it is not in the source it is credited to. What he thought about the army during the years he was in it is not on the record at all.
suggested_refs: The absent personal papers of Oberleutnant Karl Gräser, 1894-1901
sources: de.wikipedia.org, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)', full wikitext export checked 2026

segments.name: Veldes: the Cure and the Three

stops.name: Veldes, the cure at the Mallerbrunn
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] that Gräser travelled to Veldes (Bled) in the late summer of 1899 to take a cure at Arnold Rikli's naturopathic institute, apparently for serious illness (de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'). The institute's name is spelled inconsistently across the sources, Mallerbrunn in Karl's article and Mallnerbrunn in de.wikipedia's 'Ida Hofmann'; neither spelling is preferred here. Day defaulted to 01. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from ida_hoffmann.journey.json; note engelmann.journey.json pins Veldes at 46.3684/14.1147, an unreconciled divergence inside the corpus.
stops.campa: He comes to Veldes in Carniola in the late summer, an officer on leave and, the source says, seriously ill. Arnold Rikli has been running his institute beside the lake here for decades: no drugs, no instruments, sun, air, water, walking barefoot on wet grass at dawn, the body left uncovered in the light for as long as the light lasts. Rikli calls himself a Heliopath. The valley calls him the sun doctor. Gräser arrives out of a fortress in Galicia and undresses on a Slovene hillside.
suggested_refs: Arnold Rikli's Naturheilanstalt at Veldes, spelled Mallerbrunn and Mallnerbrunn in different sources

stops.name: Veldes, the three who found a common concern
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] and corrected against the research pool, which duplicated this meeting into a second entry a year late. Both de.wikipedia's 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)' and 'Ida Hofmann' place the meeting with Henri Oedenkoven and Ida Hofmann during the late-summer 1899 stay at Rikli's institute, Ida being at Bled to visit her gravely ill father. The 1900 meeting is the separate Munich-Schwabing reunion. Day defaulted to 01. The quotation is Stefan Bollmann's authorial prose about the three of them, not testimony by any of them.
stops.campa: Three patients at the same establishment. Gräser, twenty-four, an army officer for a season more. Henri Oedenkoven, the same age, son of a Belgian industrialist and heir to the money that will pay for everything. Ida Hofmann, a trained musician out of a Saxon mining family, at Bled because her father is dying there. Rikli's regimen puts all three of them out on the same hillside at the same hour every morning for weeks, unclothed in the light, with nothing to do but talk. They are unlike one another in almost every particular. What binds them, the source says, is a common concern; it does not say whose idea it was, or on which morning.
stops.quote: ein neues Leben, in dem die Herkunft wie ausradiert war und die Zukunft Gestalt annahm
stops.quote_source: Stefan Bollmann, Monte Verità 1900 (DVA, München 2017), p. 25, on the three who met at Veldes; cited on de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'
suggested_refs: The late-summer 1899 meeting of Gräser, Oedenkoven and Ida Hofmann at Rikli's institute

stops.name: Veldes, the settlement planned on the lake
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] within the corpus rather than in de.wikipedia: ida_hoffmann.journey.json and engelmann.journey.json both carry the 1899 Veldes meeting, and the corpus records that Gräser and Oedenkoven worked out there the plan for a cooperative settlement in the south. De.wikipedia does not itself date the plan to Veldes and speaks only of a shared concern. The day is a placeholder inside the attested late-summer stay.
stops.campa: What comes out of the cure is a scheme: a cooperative somewhere in the south, warm enough to live outdoors in, vegetables grown by the people who eat them, no wages and no proprietor. Oedenkoven has the capital. Ida Hofmann has the practical seriousness and the theory. Gräser has been running an association called Without Coercion out of a fortress on the San and knows better than either of them what an institution does to the people inside it. They separate at the end of the summer and write to each other.
suggested_refs: The southern vegetable cooperative projected at Veldes in 1899

stops.name: Zürich, the lectures with his brother
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] for the year: 'Im Jahr 1900 hielt Gräser zusammen mit Gusto Vorträge in Zürich' (de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'). Correction to the research pool, which credited this to de.wikipedia's 'Gustav Gräser': the full wikitext of that article contains no mention of Zurich lectures, so the joint act is recorded on Karl's side of the record and not on his brother's. No month, venue, audience or subject is given; month defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: The brothers stand up in Zurich together and speak for the reformed life. It is the only public act the record shows the two of them performing side by side before Ascona, and the record shows almost nothing of it: no hall, no month, no title, no count of who came. Gusto Gräser is twenty-one, has already broken with the family and started walking. Karl is twenty-four, and on paper he is still an officer of the Austro-Hungarian army, drawing an imperial salary in the week that he speaks.
suggested_refs: The 1900 Zurich lectures of the Gräser brothers on the reformed life

stops.name: Munich-Schwabing, the flat where it is decided
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] for autumn 1900, corrected against the research pool's 'early 1900'. De.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)', dates the reunion 'ein gutes Jahr später' than the late-summer 1899 cure, and 'Ida Hofmann' has the group leaving Munich for Ticino in the autumn of 1900. Day defaulted to 01. Further corrections to the pool: the flat was the Hofmann family's, where Ida's mother and both sisters lived; Lilly's real name was Julia and Jenny's Eugénie; Lotte Hattemer was from Berlin, her father a Bürgermeister there, and de.wikipedia's 'Ida Hofmann' calling her 'aus Stettin' is the erroneous version; Ferdinand Brune was the son of a Graz landowner, not a landowner, and was left behind because nobody but Hattemer thought him fit for the project. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from gusto_graeser.journey.json and ida_hoffmann.journey.json.
stops.campa: A good year after the lake, the party assembles in the Hofmann family's flat in Schwabing: Ida Hofmann, her mother, her sisters Julia and Eugénie who go by Lilly and Jenny, Oedenkoven up from Antwerp, Lotte Hattemer whose father is a mayor of Berlin, Ferdinand Brune from Graz, and Gusto, who arrives unannounced and is on nobody's list. Karl is there and, his own article says, already out of the army, which his own discharge date will contradict. They resolve to go south and do it.
suggested_refs: The Hofmann family flat in Munich-Schwabing, where the cooperative was constituted in autumn 1900

stops.name: Ascona, the brothers on the scouting march
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] for the Erkundungszug in late autumn 1900 (Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF); de.wikipedia and en.wikipedia date the resulting meeting with Engelmann to November 1900. Day defaulted to 01. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from engelmann.journey.json. Important correction to the research pool, which stated that no words of Karl Gräser survive anywhere: this letter, quoted in Ida Hofmann's 1906 memoir and relayed by Müller, is his, and it is the only first-person text of his located in this pass.
stops.campa: Karl and Gusto go south ahead of the others and walk the shore of Lago Maggiore looking for ground that can be bought. They ask in the villages. They find long-haired people and vegetarian boarding houses already in the district, which nobody in Munich had known about, and Karl writes north to say so. The letter is the one surviving scrap of his own voice in any source reached: three clauses, an abbreviation, and an instruction. Here one finds people, he writes, and then, come to us.
stops.quote: "Hier findet man Menschen", "auch langhaarige - vegetarische Pensionen u.s.w." schrieb Karl, "kommet zu uns"
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann, Monte Verità, p. 15, quoted in Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF
suggested_refs: The Gräser brothers' Erkundungszug along Lago Maggiore, late autumn 1900
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Monte Trinità, the pension found at dusk
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] for November 1900 (de.wikipedia and en.wikipedia on the meeting with Engelmann). Ida Hofmann's memoir gives the hour, gegen die Abendstunde, but no day; the fifteenth is a placeholder inside the attested month. Contradiction flagged and not resolved: Müller has the brothers stumbling on the pension in the course of their own search, while a rival account has Engelmann writing to Munich to summon them, and the two versions reverse the direction the information travels. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from engelmann.journey.json.
stops.campa: Above Locarno, toward the evening hour, the searchers come in on a vegetarian boarding house kept by a German named Engelmann and his wife, and are received kindly. Engelmann has been on this terrace since 1898, writing about Germanic decline. He knows the district. He knows that a theosophist called Alfredo Pioda had once meant to put a lay monastery on a hill across the water and never got past the plan. Two accounts of the evening survive and they run the information in opposite directions: in one the brothers walk in on the pension by chance, in the other Engelmann has already written to Munich to call them down.
suggested_refs: The Engelmann couple's vegetarian pension on Monte Trinità above Locarno
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Monte Monescia, the vineyard bought from Pioda
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] that Oedenkoven, Ida Hofmann, Karl and Gusto Gräser and Lotte Hattemer bought roughly four hectares of the hill from Alfredo Pioda in the late autumn of 1900 (de.wikipedia, 'Monte Verità'). Corrections to the research pool: Karl is named as one of the buying group and is nowhere credited with coordinating the acquisition; the money came 'vor allem' from Oedenkoven with Ida and Jenny Hofmann also contributing; the four hectares were reached through further purchases rather than one; and the group came overland from Munich by Oberammergau and Cadenabbia, not along the upper Italian lakes. Month set as the late edge of that autumn. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from gusto_graeser.journey.json, ida_hoffmann.journey.json and engelmann.journey.json; note that de.wikipedia's own point for Monte Verità is 46.15885/8.76287.
stops.campa: They buy the hill: four hectares of exhausted vineyard on Monte Monescia above Ascona, terraced, chestnut-shaded, with shepherds' animals on it and a view south over Lago Maggiore. The seller is Alfredo Pioda, a Ticinese who had wanted a theosophical monastery on the same slope and got no further than wanting it. Most of the money is Oedenkoven's. Karl Gräser's name stands on the list of buyers and nowhere else in the transaction. Nobody yet calls the hill the Mountain of Truth.
suggested_refs: Alfredo Pioda's unbuilt theosophical monastery on Monte Monescia, planned around 1889 with Franz Hartmann and Constance Wachtmeister

stops.name: Przemysl, the commission laid down
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] for the date, 16 September 1901, the closing end of the service span in de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'. Contradiction flagged and not resolved: the same article states that at the autumn 1900 Munich meeting Gräser was 'inzwischen aus dem Militärdienst ausgeschieden', already out of the service, which cannot be reconciled with a discharge dated nearly a year later; the two statements sit within one article and neither is withdrawn. No place is recorded for the discharge and the garrison pin is used to order the segment. The quotation about mindless regimentation often attached to this moment is not in the cited source and is not reproduced.
stops.campa: On the sixteenth of September the seven years close. He is twenty-six, out of the army, and part owner of a Swiss hillside he has already helped to buy. His own article has him out of the service a year earlier, at the Munich meeting, and gives this date for the discharge in the same account; both statements stand and neither is withdrawn. No source records where he was standing when it happened, or whether he went back to Galicia at all to sign for it. The regiment keeps no further record of him that anyone has found.
suggested_refs: The discharge of 16 September 1901 from k.u.k. Infanterieregiment Nr. 58

stops.name: Monte Verità, the light-air huts
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] that the cooperative began putting up light-air huts on the hill in 1901 and that Gräser was one of the founding group at that stage (de.wikipedia, 'Monte Verità'; de.wikipedia, 'Ida Hofmann'). The month is set to order the segment; no source dates his residence in the settlement proper, and nothing describes what he did there day to day. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus's Monte Verità pin.
stops.campa: The first year on the hill is spent putting up huts of wood and glass, one room each, open on one side, so that a body can sleep in the light and wake in it. They terrace ground for vegetables. They eat no meat, wear no wool, and nobody is paid. Oedenkoven is drawing up an accounting. Ida Hofmann is drawing up a theory of the woman question. What Gräser did on the hill day to day is described in no source consulted. Within the year he buys ground of his own next to it.
suggested_refs: The light-air huts of the first Monte Verità cooperative, 1901

stops.name: Above Ascona, the plot bought for themselves
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] that Karl Gräser and Jenny Hofmann bought their own plot near Monte Verità: 'erwarben für sich ein eigenes Grundstück in der Nähe des Monte Verità' (de.wikipedia, 'Ida Hofmann'). Correction to the research pool, which had them granted the land. The date is the letter of 10 July recorded in Karl's mother's diary announcing that he had married Jenny (gusto-graeser.info), which also warns that the same diary carries false datings; the union therefore predates the December split, against the corpus's earlier reading of a free marriage begun in December 1901. Her profession is contradictory in the sources: Karl's article calls her 'einer Pianistin und Erzieherin' in one sentence and 'die ausgebildete Opernsängerin Jenny (eigentlich: Eugénie, * 2. August 1863)' in another, while de.wikipedia's 'Ida Hofmann' independently calls her a trained opera singer, the better-attested reading used here. Note gusto-graeser.info gives her birth date as 12 August 1863, against Karl's article's 2 August. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from gusto_graeser.journey.json and ida_hoffmann.journey.json; the plot's exact position is undocumented.
stops.campa: Jenny Hofmann, born Eugénie at Kronstadt in 1863, Ida's sister and a trained opera singer, joins her life to his with no registrar and no priest. She is twelve years older than he is and was born in the same Transylvanian town. A letter of the tenth of July reaches his mother there saying that he has married. They buy ground of their own beside the cooperative, with their own money and in their own names, and move onto it. The colony is not yet a year old.
suggested_refs: The plot adjoining Monte Verità bought by Karl Gräser and Jenny Hofmann in 1901

stops.name: Monte Verità, the December parting
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] that Gräser left the Monte Verità community in December 1901 (de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'); day defaulted to 01. Contradiction flagged and not resolved: gusto_graeser.journey.json and ida_hoffmann.journey.json date Gusto's expulsion from the same community to June 1901, at the instigation of Ida Hofmann and Henri Oedenkoven, and the two brothers' departures are separately dated in the sources and may be conflated in some retellings. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus's Monte Verità pin.
stops.campa: In December he goes. The cooperative is turning into an enterprise: paying guests, a prospectus, a tariff, an accounting, rules. Gräser wants the thing the three of them described at the lake in Carniola, not the thing being built out of it. His brother had already been put out of the same settlement in June, at the instigation of Ida Hofmann and Oedenkoven. Karl is not put out. He walks over a property line onto ground he owns, and the sources keep the two departures separate, with separate dates and separate reasons.
suggested_refs: The December 1901 fracture of the first Monte Verità cooperative

stops.name: Above Ascona, prehistoric people
stops.date_confidence: attested [A]: de.wikipedia's 'Ida Hofmann' records that the pair lived in a derelict vineyard hut and presented themselves as 'prähistorische Menschen', rejecting animal and machine labour as illegitimate. The phrase is verbatim from that article and is kept as a quotation. Year set to order the segment; no source dates the move into the hut. The coordinate is the corpus placeholder for the adjoining ground and is not a surveyed point.
stops.campa: They move into an abandoned vineyard hut on their own ground and call themselves prehistoric people. No draught animal, because an animal in harness is coerced. No machine, because a machine is another man's labour congealed and bought. What is to be eaten is grown by the two pairs of hands that will eat it, dug with a spade, and what cannot be got that way is done without. The phrase is theirs, set down by Ida Hofmann five years later in a book meant to damage them. Below the property line the cooperative is putting in plumbing.
stops.quote_source: de.wikipedia.org, 'Ida Hofmann', on Karl Gräser and Jenny Hofmann in the derelict vineyard hut
suggested_refs: The derelict vineyard hut on the Gräser plot above Ascona

stops.name: Above Ascona, the life without money
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] both for the attempt and for its failure: de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)', describes 'ein radikal konsequentes Leben ohne Geld, das die beiden jedoch praktisch nie vollständig erreichten', a radically consistent life without money that the two of them never in practice fully achieved. The research pool dropped that qualifying clause. Käthe Kruse's essay on Gräser for ticinarte, from which the quotation comes, is no longer online and is quoted here only as cited on de.wikipedia. Year set to order the segment.
stops.campa: The rule is that nothing may be accepted from anyone. Not help, not a gift, not a wage, not a loan. Only what a person makes with his own strength and his own hands is fit for him to use. Oedenkoven, over the property line with his Belgian money and his paying guests, is by this measure not living the life at all. Neither, in the end, are they. The source that records the attempt records in the same sentence that the two of them never in practice fully reached it, and does not say where the line broke.
stops.quote: Gräsers gingen in ihren Theorien noch viel weiter als Oedenkoven. Sie verschmähten jede Hilfe. Nur was der Mensch mit seiner eigenen Kraft, mit seiner eigenen Hände Arbeit sich schaffen könne, sei ihm gemäss und gut.
stops.quote_source: Käthe Kruse, essay on Karl Gräser, ticinarte (page no longer online), as cited on de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'

stops.name: Above Ascona, Erich Mühsam comes up the hill
stops.date_confidence: attested [A]: Erich Mühsam, Ascona (Verlag Birger Carlson, Locarno, 1905), p. 40, as cited on de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'. The book's imprint year is 1905 and the encounter is undated within it, so the year is the imprint's and the month is defaulted to 01. This is a contemporary's direct testimony about Karl specifically, distinct from anything said of Gusto, and is one of only two independent contemporary verdicts on him located in this pass. Coordinate is the Gräser plot rather than Ascona town; Mühsam came to the colonists.
stops.campa: The anarchist writer Erich Mühsam spends part of a year among the Ascona colonists and publishes a small book about them in Locarno, mostly unimpressed by what he finds. The book is called simply Ascona and runs to a few dozen pages. On Gräser he is favourable, and what he praises is method and not doctrine: not that the man is right, but that he puts into practice, with rigid consistency, whatever he has worked out to be right. Mühsam nowhere says the theory is correct.
stops.quote: Gräser ist der erste Mensch, der mir begegnet ist, der mit starrer Konsequenz das, was er theoretisch als richtig erkannt hat, in die Praxis umsetzt.
stops.quote_source: Erich Mühsam, Ascona (Verlag Birger Carlson, Locarno, 1905), p. 40
suggested_refs: Erich Mühsam, Ascona (Locarno, 1905), the earliest published outsider account of the colonists

stops.name: Above Ascona, the sister's verdict
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] and verified against the primary source rather than only through de.wikipedia: Ida Hofmann, Monte Verita: Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (Karl Rohm, Lorch, 1906), p. 96, archive.org item MonteVeritaWahrheitOD, OCR confirmed, where the OCR reads 'rem' for 'rein'. Corrections to the research pool: the passage concerns one woman, her own sister Jenny, not women drawn into a household; the setting is Gräser's own adjoining ground, not Monte Verità itself; and the fragment as usually quoted is not a sentence, its main verb arriving much later, so the ellipsis is marked. Hofmann is a hostile witness inside a factional split, writing about her sister. Karl's own article separately paraphrases her as lamenting the mental and physical decline that came out of the union; the phrasings sometimes attributed to her about suggestive power reducing her sister to a helpless instrument of deranged views are not in either article. Year is the imprint's; month defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: Ida Hofmann publishes her account of the mountain with a press in Württemberg, and on page ninety-six she turns to her sister's partner. She had stood beside him at the lake in Carniola seven years earlier and walked south with him into Ticino. Now she writes that he has bound the woman who entrusted herself to him into his fanaticism to satisfy purely selfish ends, that his pride is barely broken, and that what may be a pathological lying darkens his ways for the present.
stops.quote: Die suggestive Kraft, mit welcher er das sich ihm anvertrauende Weib zur Befriedigung rein egoistischer Zwecke in seinen Fanatismus zu verstricken... Karl Gräser's Stolz ist kaum merklich gebrochen; hervorragende Eigenliebe, ein vielleicht pathologisches Lügnertum verdunkeln vorläufig seine Wege.
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann, Monte Verita: Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (Karl Rohm, Lorch, 1906), p. 96; the ellipsis marks omitted continuation
suggested_refs: Ida Hofmann, Monte Verita: Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (Lorch, 1906), archive.org item MonteVeritaWahrheitOD

stops.name: Monte Verità, Casa Francesco built
stops.date_confidence: attested [A]: de.wikipedia, 'Monte Verità', identifies Karl Gräser's house on the hill as Casa Francesco, built in Heimatschutzstil by the architect Paul Evertz and decorated with two frescoes by Alexander Wilhelm de Beauclair. The research pool's afterlife lens dates the building to 1903-1906 and the year here opens that span; no source gives a completion date. Contradiction flagged and not resolved: a named architect, a stone house in a self-conscious regional style and a fresco painter sit badly against the moneyless prehistoric-people regime recorded for the same ground in the same years, and nothing consulted reconciles them.
stops.campa: A house goes up on the hill with a name, Casa Francesco, built in the Heimatschutz manner by an architect called Paul Evertz, with two frescoes on it by Alexander Wilhelm de Beauclair. It is Karl Gräser's. The man who will take no help and no wage has an architect and a fresco painter working on his house, and the house is standing a century later with a name on the plans. Nothing in any accessible source explains how the vineyard hut and the commissioned house occupy the same slope in the same decade.
suggested_refs: Casa Francesco on Monte Verità, by Paul Evertz, with frescoes by Alexander Wilhelm de Beauclair

stops.name: Losone, the cave in the rocks
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction [R]. De.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)', records a Gräser-Höhle, a rock cave dwelling near Losone by Ascona, as a surviving trace of his ascetic way of life after December 1901. No source dates his use of it, gives a period of residence, or distinguishes it from the Arcegno cave associated with his brother in gusto_graeser.journey.json, which sits at 46.1714749/8.7354549. The year is set only to order the segment and the coordinate is the research pool's, not a surveyed point.
stops.campa: There is a cave in the rock near Losone, above Ascona, that carries the family name and is shown as his. Whether he slept in it for a season or a decade, whether it was shelter or discipline or simply a place to be out of sight of the sanatorium's paying guests, nothing on the record says. No date is attached to it, no period of residence, no witness. His brother had a cave of his own on the same range, an hour's walk off, and it is the brother's that the visitors climbed up to and wrote about afterwards.
suggested_refs: The Gräser-Höhle near Losone, above Ascona

stops.name: Locarno, the exhibition with his brother
stops.date_confidence: attested [A]: '1906/07 machten die Brüder gemeinsam eine Kunstausstellung in Locarno' (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'); de.wikipedia's 'Monte Verità' dates it to the winter of 1906/1907. The research pool's flat '1906' is corrected to that winter span and December is set as its opening. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from gusto_graeser.journey.json. Contradiction flagged and not resolved: joint work with Gusto in the winter of 1906/07 sits uneasily against Karl's December 1901 departure from the community, and no source explains whether he stayed on the hill continuously or returned to it.
stops.campa: Over the winter the two brothers hang an exhibition of pictures in Locarno. Gusto Gräser has been painting since his Vienna years; Ernst, the youngest, is a painter and graphic artist by trade. It is the second recorded occasion on which Karl and Gusto do anything publicly together, six years after the Zurich lectures. Karl had left the community five years earlier and no source explains whether he stayed on the hill through those years or came back to it. Which pictures hung, whose they were, and whether anyone bought one, no source says.
suggested_refs: The Gräser brothers' Locarno art exhibition, winter 1906/07

stops.name: Monte Verità, Ascona's first gallery
stops.date_confidence: attested [A]: 'Aus ihr entstand Asconas erste Gemäldegalerie im Hause von Karl Gräser' (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'), and de.wikipedia's 'Monte Verità' places the permanent gallery in Casa Francesco on the hill, correcting the research pool's Ascona-town placement and coordinate. It also records that the gallery drew Viennese and German artists in the summer months. Day and month defaulted to 01, at the close of the 1906/07 winter.
stops.campa: The pictures do not go back into store. They stay, in Casa Francesco, and the house becomes the first permanent painting gallery in the district: Viennese and German artists showing there through the summer months, visitors climbing up from the lake to see canvases hung in a private house on a hill famous for people who eat raw vegetables. Every other undertaking on his record he joined; this one is his, in his own rooms. The accounts left by the people who came up to see the pictures do not name him.
suggested_refs: Ascona's first permanent painting gallery, in Casa Francesco on Monte Verità

stops.name: Monte Verità, the years with nothing in them
stops.date_confidence: gap statement [R]. Between the 1906/07 gallery and the illness recorded for 1915, no accessible source places Karl Gräser anywhere, records anything he did, or names anyone who saw him. De.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)', has him at the Gräser-Haus on Monte Verità until 1915, which is a statement of residence and not of activity. The year is set only to order the segment.
stops.campa: Eight years pass on the hill and the paper holds nothing at all. The colony fills with strangers in these years, dancers and fasters and theosophists and psychoanalysts, and the accounts they leave behind name his brother and his brother's grotto and never him. The gallery is in his house and no visitor's account of it names the man whose house it is. The house stands, the ground is his, he is recorded as living on it, and for eight years nobody writes down one thing Karl Gräser says or does. Then, in 1915, he falls ill.
suggested_refs: The Gräser-Haus on Monte Verità, recorded as his residence until 1915

segments.name: Nassau, Kassel, and the Contested Year

stops.name: Monte Verità, the illness of 1915
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] that he fell seriously ill in 1915 and remained at the Gräser-Haus on Monte Verità until then (de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'). No month, no diagnosis and no place of onset are given; month defaulted to 01. Noted and not stated as fact: gusto-graeser.info says he became 'gemütskrank' and ended in an asylum as Jenny did, and that he 'soll vor seinem Tode seine früheren Überzeugungen widerrufen haben', is said to have recanted his earlier convictions before his death. Both are marked in that source as report and are hearsay.
stops.campa: In 1915 he falls seriously ill. The record gives the year and nothing else: no diagnosis, no doctor, no description of what the illness does to him. It is the fifteenth year on the mountain and the second year of a war that has emptied the colony of its foreigners. Within a year he will be off the mountain and out of Switzerland altogether, in a country at war, in other people's houses. One source, a family site, says he became sick in his mind and ended in an asylum as Jenny did, and marks its own sentence as report rather than fact.
suggested_refs: gusto-graeser.info, 'Karl Gräser (13.8.1875 - 28.10.1916)', which transcribes the Kassel register and reports the asylum tradition

stops.name: Nassau an der Lahn, nursed by the youngest sister
stops.date_confidence: attested [A]: 'Gräser wurde zunächst bis Anfang August 1916 in Nassau an der Lahn von Lilly Brepohl (geborene Hofmann) gepflegt' (de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'). Lilly, real name Julia, was Jenny's and Ida's youngest sister, married to the Protestant pastor Friedrich Wilhelm Brepohl, with whom she later emigrated to Brazil. Coordinate corrected: the research pool's 50.1969/7.8163 lies about 13 km south-southeast of the town in open country in the Taunus foothills and does not point at Nassau at all; the pin is Nassau (Lahn) itself per de.wikipedia. No date is given for his arrival there, so the month is set to order the segment; only the end of the stay, the first days of August 1916, is attested.
stops.campa: He is in Germany, in a small town on the Lahn, in the third year of the war, being nursed by Julia Brepohl, called Lilly, the youngest of the three Hofmann sisters, married to a Protestant pastor. She was in the Schwabing flat in 1900 when the whole thing was decided. Sixteen years on she is changing the bedding of the man her sister went to live with in a vineyard hut. How he crossed a wartime frontier from Ticino to the Lahn, and who paid for it, is not recorded anywhere. He is under her care until the first days of August.
suggested_refs: The household of Pastor Friedrich Wilhelm Brepohl and Julia 'Lilly' Brepohl née Hofmann at Nassau an der Lahn

stops.name: Kassel, Kohlenstrasse 350
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] from the Kassel Melderegister as transcribed by gusto-graeser.info, which is the footnote de.wikipedia actually cites for this passage rather than Bollmann: Eugenie 'Jenny' Gräser geb. Hofmann, born 12 August 1863 at Kronstadt, registered at Kohlenstr. 350 bei Grossmann, Kassel-Wilhelmshöhe, on 14 June 1916; Karl, entered as 'Gutsbesitzer ungarischer Nationalität', moved into the same house on 12 August 1916, coming from Nassau an der Lahn. Correction to the research pool, which had the two of them moving together and inferred a motive of nearer medical care: he moves alone, away from his nurse, to where Jenny already lived. No source gives any motive.
stops.campa: Jenny has been registered in Kassel since the fourteenth of June, in a lodging house on the Kohlenstrasse out at Wilhelmshöhe. On the twelfth of August, which is her birthday, he moves into the same house, coming from Nassau an der Lahn. He is forty-one, he owns a hill in Switzerland, he has spent fifteen years refusing to touch money, and he is a lodger in a rented room in a German city in the middle of a war. The clerk enters him in the register as Gutsbesitzer ungarischer Nationalität: landowner, Hungarian national.
suggested_refs: The Kassel Melderegister entries for Kohlenstrasse 350, Kassel-Wilhelmshöhe, June and August 1916
sources: gusto-graeser.info, 'Karl Gräser (13.8.1875 - 28.10.1916)', transcribing the Kassel Melderegister

stops.name: Kassel, the marriage of the twenty-eighth of September
stops.date_confidence: attested [A]: 'Am 28. September 1916 haben die beiden geheiratet' (gusto-graeser.info, transcribing the Kassel record; cited on de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'). Correction to the corpus: this is not the formalising of a free marriage begun in December 1901, which is when the pair separated from Oedenkoven and Ida Hofmann; Karl's mother's diary records a letter of 10 July 1901 announcing that he had married Jenny, so the partnership predates the split by months. No source gives a reason for the 1916 wedding.
stops.campa: After fifteen years without a registrar they marry in Kassel. Everything that union was for, the refusal of state form and of church form, the arrangement answerable to nobody, is signed into a civil register six weeks before he dies. Nobody wrote down why. Nobody has produced the certificate itself either, only the register's line about it. A widow's claim, a foreign national's papers in wartime, a hospital wanting a next of kin, a Swiss hillside that will shortly need an owner: any of them would serve, and no source names one.
suggested_refs: The Kassel civil marriage record of Karl Gräser and Eugenie Hofmann, 28 September 1916

stops.name: Kassel, the twenty-eighth of October
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] as the strongest evidence available: 'Vier Wochen später, am 28. Oktober 1916, ist Karl Gräser gestorben' (gusto-graeser.info, from the Kassel register; cited on de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'). He was 41, which is arithmetically consistent with the 1875 birth. No cause of death is given in any source consulted, and no burial place is described anywhere. The date is contradicted in print elsewhere and that contradiction is carried in the following stop rather than resolved here. Note also that the death falls inside the First World War but is not a war death: the illness is dated 1915 and began in Switzerland.
stops.campa: Four weeks after the wedding, on the twenty-eighth of October 1916, he dies in Kassel at forty-one. The war he dies inside has nothing to do with it; the illness is a year old and began on a Swiss hillside. Jenny is in the same house. His brother Gusto, condemned to death at Kronstadt for refusing to serve in this same war, is alive. No cause is entered in anything reachable, no doctor is named, no funeral is described, and no grave is described either.
suggested_refs: The Kassel death record of Karl Gräser, 28 October 1916

stops.name: Kassel, the year that will not settle
stops.date_confidence: contradiction, flagged and not resolved. The Kassel Melderegister as transcribed by gusto-graeser.info gives 28 October 1916 and is the strongest evidence. The SAME page's biographical header reads '† 1920 wahrscheinlich in Kassel' and 'Er starb 1920, wahrscheinlich in Kassel'. The archived ticinARTE page gives '1875-1915, gestorben in Ascona'. De.wikipedia's own Weblinks flag that the Wiener Zeitung of 28 June 2020 gives 1920. And gusto-graeser.info warns that the Hofmann family diary carries 'Falschdatierungen... hauptsächlich falsche Angaben zu seinem Todesjahr'. The 1920 date here is the alternative in print, pinned to carry the dispute, and is not an assertion.
stops.campa: Three years are in print for his death and two places. 1915 in Ascona, on an art site now offline. 1916 in Kassel, out of the city's own register. 1920 in Kassel, probably, in the header of the very page that transcribes the 1916 register underneath it, and again in a Viennese newspaper as late as 2020. The family diary that ought to settle it is known to carry false dates, and the false dates it carries are mostly about the year Karl Gräser died.
suggested_refs: The divided literature on Karl Gräser's death year: Kassel 1916, Kassel 1920, Ascona 1915

segments.name: What Is Left on the Hill

stops.name: Monte Verità, the estate after him
stops.date_confidence: contradiction, flagged and not resolved. De.wikipedia's 'Gustav Gräser' dates Gusto's residence with his own family on Karl's property at Monte Verità to 1916-1918, a span that opens in the year of Karl's October death and that neither article reconciles with it. What the passage does establish is that Karl held real property on the hill in his own name and that others used it after him. Month set to order the segment.
stops.campa: The ground stays in the family. Gusto and his household live on his dead brother's property at Monte Verità from 1916 to 1918, which is how it is known that Karl held real property there in his own name at all. The two encyclopedia articles carrying these dates do not reconcile them with an October 1916 death and do not remark on the difficulty. Neither says who inherited the ground, or on what paper, or what Jenny was supposed to do with a Swiss hillside from a rented room in Kassel. The house with the frescoes on it is still there.
suggested_refs: The Gräser property on Monte Verità, occupied by Gusto Gräser's family 1916-1918

stops.name: Casa Anatta, the chair
stops.date_confidence: attested [A] as an object on display: de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)', records that his chair survives and is shown at the Museo Casa Anatta, the Monte Verità history museum. No acquisition date, provenance chain or catalogue number is given by the source, and no photograph was located; the year is set only to order the segment. Coordinate for Casa Anatta inherited byte-identical from ida_hoffmann.journey.json.
stops.campa: In the museum on the hill, among the photographs of naked dancers and the drawings of light-air huts, there is a chair. It was his. He left no book, no poem and no doctrine, and no grave of his has been found, so the chair is the object that carries his name. A man who held that a machine is congealed coercion and an animal in harness a slave sat on a thing somebody made. The source that records it gives no acquisition date, no provenance, no catalogue number and no photograph, and it stands in the room under a label.
suggested_refs: Karl Gräser's chair, Museo Casa Anatta, Monte Verità

stops.name: Monte Verità, no grave and one clipped line
stops.date_confidence: gap statement [R]. No accessible source describes Karl Gräser's grave, tomb, burial place or any memorial naming him, at Kassel or anywhere else; this is a gap in the sources consulted, not a finding that no grave exists. The German Wikipedia disambiguation page for the name carries him in a single line, 'deutsch-österreichischer Offizier und Aussteiger', an encyclopedic descriptor and not period testimony. Correction to the research pool on the literature: Stefan Bollmann's Monte Verità 1900 (DVA, München 2017, ISBN 978-3-421-04685-7) is real and heavily cited on de.wikipedia's 'Ida Hofmann', but does NOT appear in the Literatur of Karl's own article, which lists Hofmann 1906, Adolf Grohmann 1904 and Andreas Schwab, Monte Verità: Sanatorium der Sehnsucht (Orell Füssli, Zürich 2003). Year set to order the segment.
stops.campa: The disambiguation page gives him one line: German-Austrian officer and dropout. There is no grave on record anywhere, which is a hole in the sources rather than a fact about the ground. His brother has a legend, poems signed O.Z., a rescued estate and a scholar who spent a career on him. Karl has a service record, two land purchases, a residency card, a marriage certificate, a chair, and one letter of his own telling the others in Munich to come south.
